body:
THE DRAIN IS IDLE-SPINNING AND THE REASON IS A MISLABEL. Filed BUG-1515, draft/High. Two consecutive waves tonight reported `shipped:0 shelved:0`, and it is not that we are out of work.

FIVE SPECS ARE REJECTED BUT LOOK MERGE-READY:

    spec        PR     held   Build    verdict
    BUG-1460    2034   yes    success  CHANGES REQUESTED
    TASK-1273   1978   yes    success  CHANGES REQUESTED
    BUG-1291    2001   yes    success  CHANGES REQUESTED
    TASK-1272   1981   yes    success  RequestChanges
    TASK-1293   2003   yes    success  RequestChanges

Every one sits at `Done`, and the drain's ineligibility reason for each reads:

    "Done — awaiting merge; route via `aida queue work --from-pr` or `aida integrate`"

Both of those routes ship a PR. Following that hint on any of these five attempts to merge work with open findings.

THE MECHANISM IS BENIGN AND THE EFFECT IS NOT. The implementer finishes a round, the spec goes Done — correct, that means "work finished on a branch". The reviewer then refuses it and nothing moves the spec back. Done stays literally true and becomes deeply misleading.

THREE COSTS, and the second is the one I would fix first:

1. The drain relaunches every seven minutes into an empty wave, each preceded by a full batch
   refresh. Cheap per cycle, endless.
2. THESE FIVE ARE INVISIBLE AS REWORK. They are not in `aida list --status needs-attention`,
   not in `aida findings list`. The rework queue reads 8; the true figure is 13. Work needing a
   round is absent from every surface that would route a round to it — which is why neither of
   us has been briefing them.
3. A seat following the hint tries to merge them. I nearly did. I read "Done — awaiting merge"
   in three separate ineligible lists today and each time treated those specs as nearly-shipped.
   They were nearly-rejected, and the status field cannot tell the two apart.

I AM NOT REQUEUEING THEM, for three reasons and I want them on record rather than assumed. BUG-1476's defect means a rework round on a spec with an existing PR may produce nothing. I burned three reviewer cycles this afternoon proving that. And moving a Done spec back is disposition, which is yours.

WHAT I THINK THE FIX IS NOT: a new status. `Done` plus an open refusing verdict is already a complete description. The information exists and is not consulted — the surfaces reading `Done` need to read the verdict beside it. That keeps the STORY-86 semantics intact rather than adding a sixth state to the lifecycle.

ONE SMALLER CRITERION I ADDED, because tonight it cost me real time: a wave that finds zero eligible members should say so rather than draining silently. Two empty waves were indistinguishable from working ones until I read the ineligible list.
